drug_indication: MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis
catalyst_text: Presented positive real world MASH outcomes at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: Multiple real-world studies presented at AASLD reported improvements or stabilization in liver stiffness and favorable changes in liver and cardiometabolic biomarkers among adults with MASH with moderate to advanced fibrosis treated in routine U.S. practice. Persistence at one year reached up to 72% with high adherence, and safety was consistent with prior clinical experience. These data support real-world effectiveness and tolerability after approval.
catalyst_text_evidence: CONSHOHOCKEN, Pa., 2026-11-05 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ:MDGL), a biopharmaceutical company focused on delivering novel therapeutics for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), today announced results from multiple real-world studies of Rezdiffra presented at the American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD) The Liver Meeting, taking place 2026-11-05–2026-11-09 in Denver. Across multiple independent real-world data sources, patients achieved meaningful improvements (based on a 25% threshold) or stabilization in liver stiffness measurements, a noninvasive marker associated with liver fibrosis, approximately one year after treatment initiation. Treatment persistence studies showed up to 72% of patients remained on Rezdiffra at one year, with high adherence. Safety findings were consistent with the established safety profile of Rezdiffra observed in clinical trials. Across studies, approximately 37% to 55% of patients with paired measurements achieved a ≥25% improvement in liver stiffness after approximately one year; most improved or remained stable.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 analyses at EASL Congress
detailed_catalyst_text: New Phase 3 analyses and multiple real-world studies in MASH were presented at EASL 2026, showing significant reductions in atherogenic lipids and achievement of key histologic endpoints regardless of baseline statin use. In well‑compensated MASH cirrhosis, an open‑label extension showed progressive reductions in ANTICIPATE‑NASH risk scores, and real‑world cohorts demonstrated early and sustained improvements in liver biomarkers and stiffness. These findings support potential reductions in cardiovascular and liver‑related risk and provide guidance for routine clinical practice.
catalyst_text_evidence: “Madrigal Pharmaceuticals, Inc. … today announced new analyses of Phase 3 data and real-world evidence demonstrating Rezdiffra reduced markers of cardiovascular and liver-related risk in patients with MASH. The data are featured across eight poster presentations at the European Association for the Study of the Liver (EASL) Congress 2026, taking place 2026-05-27 to 2026-05-30 in Barcelona, Spain.” “Data from a secondary analysis of the Phase 3 MAESTRO-NASH and MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 trials demonstrated that Rezdiffra improved key histologic MASH endpoints and significantly reduced multiple atherogenic lipids and lipoproteins associated with cardiovascular risk, including LDL-C and Lp(a), regardless of baseline statin use.” “The ANTICIPATE-NASH risk model was applied to the open-label extension (OLE) cohort from the MAESTRO-NAFLD-1 trial… Results demonstrated progressive improvements in ANTICIPATE-NASH risk scores over time.” “Multiple real-world studies evaluating patients treated with Rezdiffra for up to 12 months in routine clinical practice are also being presented at EASL. Collectively, these studies demonstrated that patients achieved clinically meaningful improvements in biomarkers of liver disease and cardiometabolic risk.”

drug_indication: Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) with liver fibrosis (also known as MASH)

catalyst_text: The analysis of primary data from Phase 3 over a 52-week period indicated that the treatment was safe, well tolerated, and resulted in substantial decreases in liver fat, as reported on June 27, 2022.
On February 8, 2018, the top-line data for Phase 2 was published, indicating that the primary endpoint was achieved.
